study_design: Prospective cohort analysis with diet assessed at entry and prostate cancer follow-up through 2004
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Subjects were a cohort of 1985 men previously to asbestos who participated in a cancer prevention programme of beta-carotene and retinol supplements that commenced in July 1990.
reason: The abstract reports incident prostate cancer overall during cohort follow-up but does not analyze an aggressive, advanced, high-grade, metastatic, or lethal incident endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Prostate cancer risk was examined in relation to intakes of fruit, vegetables, beta-carotene and retinol.
estimate_classifications.reason: The beta-carotene row concerns overall prostate cancer risk; no aggressive endpoint is established.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Fruit, other vegetables and vitamin A intakes did not appear to be strong factors in the development of prostate cancer in this study.
estimate_classifications.reason: The vitamin A row concerns development of prostate cancer overall, with no aggressive endpoint reported.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: A decreased prostate cancer risk was observed with increasing intakes of vitamin C-rich vegetables, including bell peppers and broccoli.
estimate_classifications.reason: The bell-pepper association is reported for prostate cancer overall, not aggressive disease.
